executiveSummary: Surveillance data from ECDC and PAHO spanning late 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent communicable disease threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1), a BSL-3 select agent, has generated repeated epidemiological updates in the Americas region, signaling sustained zoonotic transmission risk and potential for human spillover events. The Southern Hemisphere is entering its seasonal influenza period while the Americas simultaneously contend with dengue, chikungunya, measles, mpox, pertussis, yellow fever, and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome. The breadth and simultaneity of these threats indicate significant strain on regional public health surveillance and response capacity.
bottomLine: Multiple concurrent epidemic threats across the Americas—anchored by sustained H5N1 zoonotic activity and resurging vaccine-preventable diseases—demand coordinated regional response and heightened surveillance through mid-2026.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Repeated PAHO epidemiological updates in November 2025 and March 2026 indicate sustained and evolving H5N1 activity
Zoonotic spillover risk elevated with ongoing animal reservoir activity across multiple countries
BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential requiring immediate containment monitoring
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance protocols, increase human case screening in exposed populations, coordinate with FAO and OIE on animal reservoir control, ensure stockpile readiness for antiviral countermeasures

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 indicating active transmission in the Americas
BSL-3 classified pathogen with documented human-to-human transmission capacity
Ongoing global clade activity increases importation risk across the region
threats.action: Strengthen case detection and contact tracing, promote vaccine deployment in high-risk communities, reinforce cross-border notification and laboratory diagnostic capacity

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active cases or elevated risk
BSL-3 select agent with sylvatic and urban transmission cycles
Vaccination coverage gaps in endemic zones increase outbreak vulnerability
threats.action: Assess vaccination coverage in at-risk populations, intensify entomological surveillance for Aedes and Haemagogus vectors, enforce vaccination requirements for travelers entering endemic zones

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 2026 with documented multi-country circulation
Historically high dengue activity in prior seasons increases likelihood of sustained 2026 burden
Aedes aegypti vector range expansion linked to climate factors amplifies transmission risk
threats.action: Intensify integrated vector management, enhance hospital surge capacity planning in endemic countries, accelerate rollout of dengue vaccination where approved

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO alerts issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained resurgence
Waning immunity and vaccine hesitancy contributing to outbreak amplification
Multi-country spread pattern suggests regional rather than localized transmission
threats.action: Strengthen booster vaccination campaigns especially for adolescents and adults, enhance maternal Tdap vaccination programs, increase laboratory confirmation capacity for respiratory illness clusters

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active cases in a region previously declared measles-free
Vaccination coverage gaps post-COVID-19 pandemic creating susceptible cohorts
High transmissibility (R0 12-18) makes rapid spread likely in under-vaccinated communities
threats.action: Launch targeted supplementary immunization activities in low-coverage areas, activate outbreak investigation protocols for all confirmed cases, reinforce measles surveillance at points of entry

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 2025 indicating elevated case counts
Andes virus strain capable of person-to-person transmission in South America
Seasonal rodent population dynamics may be driving increased human exposure
threats.action: Enhance rodent control programs in endemic rural areas, issue public health advisories for high-risk occupational and recreational exposures, ensure clinical awareness for early case recognition in emergency departments

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active transmission
Aedes vector co-circulation with dengue creates compounded arboviral burden
Geographic expansion into previously unaffected areas increases novel population susceptibility
threats.action: Integrate chikungunya surveillance with existing dengue vector control programs, strengthen clinical diagnostic capacity to differentiate arboviral syndromes, monitor for neurological complications in affected populations

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents are active in the current surveillance period. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) has generated multiple PAHO epidemiological updates (November 2025 and March 2026), reflecting sustained zoonotic transmission across the Americas with pandemic spillover risk—rated Critical. Monkeypox virus (MPXV), also BSL-3 classified, shows active regional transmission documented in an April 2026 PAHO update—rated Elevated. Yellow fever virus, a BSL-3 pathogen, triggered a March 2026 PAHO alert suggesting active risk in sylvatic zones. All three require high-containment laboratory handling and coordinated public health response under applicable select agent regulations.

diseases: Multiple communicable disease threats (ECDC weekly reports Weeks 16-20 2026)

amrSignals: Bordetella pertussis strains with macrolide resistance have been documented globally; resurgent pertussis outbreaks increase selection pressure and potential for AMR strain amplification in the Americas

No explicit AMR reports identified in available report titles; absence of description data limits AMR signal extraction—active surveillance for resistant influenza strains (oseltamivir resistance) should accompany H5N1 monitoring
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen resurgence across the Americas suggests systemic immunization coverage erosion, likely a legacy effect of COVID-19 pandemic disruption to routine vaccination programs
Co-circulation of multiple arboviruses (dengue, chikungunya, Zika risk) amplified by Aedes vector expansion creates compounded diagnostic and clinical management challenges
Repeated H5N1 epidemiological updates across a 4-month span (November 2025 to March 2026) indicate the zoonotic interface remains highly active, with incrementally increasing pandemic risk
Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset (April 2026 PAHO alert) overlapping with Northern Hemisphere late-season activity creates a continuous hemispheric influenza transmission corridor
Five consecutive ECDC weekly threat reports (Weeks 16-20, April-May 2026) suggest sustained multi-threat environment in Europe requiring continued monitoring for importation events from the Americas
